title: Scheduler rebalancing and memory-aware batching for mixed prompt/response lengths
creator: Amelia Chen
description:
Problem: For mixed workloads where prompt lengths and expected response lengths vary widely (single-shot short prompts vs. multi-turn long generations), our continuous batching scheduler currently creates batches that either blow past GPU memory headroom or cause severe tail latency for short requests. This ticket drives tuning experiments and scheduler changes to balance p50/p95/p99 latency targets while maximizing overall throughput and minimizing additional GPU memory usage.

Scope: 1) scheduler rebalancing heuristics for mixed-length traffic, 2) KV cache management policies to reclaim memory for long-response bursts without impacting short queries, 3) GPU memory-aware batching window and admission controls, and 4) rollout and observability to detect regressions.

Non-goals: full reimplementation of the runtime, major model architecture changes, or changes that require tenant-side prompt annotations (we can consider optional hints later).
acceptance_criteria: No more than 10% increase in median latency for short (<128 token) requests in experiment traffic
p95 latency for short requests improved by >= 20% compared to baseline in steady-state mixed traffic
GPU memory headroom incidents (OOMs or kernel failures) reduced to zero in canary cluster over 48h
KV cache hit rate for hot prefixes remains within 5% of baseline for high-frequency routes
Clear dashboard panels showing batch size distribution, per-shard GPU memory utilization, and per-length lane latencies
proposed_experiments: Dynamic-length bucketing: maintain short/medium/long admission lanes; short lane max batch latency target = 50ms, long lane max batching window = 200ms
Memory-aware batching window: compute per-GPU available headroom and shrink the batching window proactively when available memory < threshold (default 1.5GB) to prevent KV eviction thrash
KV eviction policy variant A (LRU-prefixed): preferentially evict large KV segments from inactive long sequences and keep hot prefixes pinned; variant B: time-decay + size budget cap
Hybrid packing: allow small short queries to be packed with long prompt prefixes if packing cost < 10% additional latency for short lane (controlled by admission lambda)
Adaptive continuous batcher: introduce a weight decay on sequence length when computing batch selection priority so extremely long responses don’t monopolize the batch window
Offload probe: evaluate pinned CPU buffer offload for rarely-hit KV shards to free GPU memory, measure effect on p95 for long generations
metrics_to_track: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency broken down by request length bucket
batch size distribution (tokens and requests) by lane
GPU memory used vs headroom (per-GPU metric) and OOM count
KV cache memory usage and hit/miss rate by prefix age
throughput (tokens/sec) and cost-per-token estimate during experiments
tail scheduling delay (time between arrival and batch formation)
percent of requests served by fallback model variant due to memory constraints
rollout_plan: 1) Local dev experiments with synthetic mixed-length workload (unit tests + perf harness)
2) Canary on runtime-cluster-canary (2 GPUs per shard) with 5% of production traffic for 48h
3) Monitor dashboards and SLO alerts; if any p99 or OOM alerts fire, rollback to baseline
4) Gradual ramp to 20/50/100% with gating at each step and 24h observation windows
5) Post-rollout: schedule follow-up re-tuning based on real traffic distributions and telemetry

2025-02-12 Diego Ramos: Added initial experiment matrix; will prototype dynamic-length buckets in the local perf harness. Need a small telemetry change to report per-request length bucket—filed ENG-9650 to add that metric.
2025-02-14 Priya Nair (SRE): Can help set up canary and alerting. Suggest adding a safety admission control that rejects or routes to dedicated capacity when free memory < 800MB.

2025-02-16 Diego Ramos: Prototype shows 18% p95 improvement for short lane under synthetic 70/20/10 short/medium/long mix with Dynamic-length bucketing + weight decay. KV eviction variant B reduced memory oscillation but increased KV misses by 3%.

2025-02-18 Amelia Chen: Decision log: proceed with Memory-aware batching window + Dynamic lanes as phase 1, KV eviction variant B as opt-in toggle. Offload probe scheduled as phase 2. Need product sign-off for admission control behavior when memory is low.
2025-02-20 Diego Ramos: Started canary rollout (5%). Telemetry dashboard updated. Observing initial stability; short-lane p95 down ~22%, total tokens/sec down ~4% (expected trade-off).
